prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale EO ground segment. Security: least privilege, strong auth, segmentation, continuous audit. Mission Control Center (MCC, Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule/routing and routine-ops authority boundary; elevated access only with approved shift role + time-limited need; sends constraints to MPS; escalation lead→discipline lead→mission mgmt. FD deliveries carry validity, frame, generation time, use statement. Flight Dynamics Facility (FDF, Mistral): orbit catalog; ephemerides/events to MCC, MPS, PPF; Star Tracker Mask File; Ephemeris Delta Note; maneuver recs to Spacecraft Operations Team (SOT); geometry to Payload Calibration Team (PCT); orbit quality changes to archive queue before catalogue flags. Payload Processing Facility (PPF, Forgehouse): Primary/Backup Processing Clusters, failover; both down→suspend, raw staged, notify MCC; recovery contractual-latency first. Telemetry Ingest Service; Pass Replay Packet (SOT uses for anomaly reconstruction). Levels L0–L2 record build/calibration/ancillary versions. PCT owns calibration baseline, may request reprocessing; assesses product integrity in anomalies. Product Quality Service (PQS): quality flags, Product Hold List, public quality status, records reprocessing reason (scientific vs operational recovery). Long Term Archive (Granite): authoritative repository; admits after PPF package+quality metadata+checksum; persistent IDs; Storage Watermark Snapshot; publishes catalogue (baseline, sensing/publication time, quality status, replacement links) to User Services Portal after PQS/embargo; preserves replaced versions unless policy consolidation; retention rules. User Services Portal: search, subscription, order, download status via versioned contracts; shows service status message if archive misses commitment, then incident process. Cybersecurity Desk: reviews public interface changes and privileged access daily; coordination authority for security anomalies. Network Control System (Lantern): enforces routing, logs config changes; Security Exception Ticket. Mission Planning System (MPS, Cedar): command package to MCC; retroreflector window only within approved interval. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): accepts mask file only if integrity, config ID, operator approval match baseline. Anomaly classification: safety, command authority, data custody, continuity, user commitments; triage: SOT spacecraft, Ground Network Manager antenna/link/site, Flight Dynamics Team orbit/timing. Orbit Determination Engine.

New part:
S213: During triage, operators preserve volatile logs, current configuration state, operator console history, and relevant message identifiers before restarting services or changing routing.
S214: Evidence is stored in write-protected case storage with a chain of custody entry that identifies the collector, collection time, source system, and reason for capture.
S215: Forgehouse must quarantine suspect input and derived output when product lineage cannot be proven during an active anomaly investigation.
S216: Cedar suspends automatic schedule publication when a security or continuity anomaly could invalidate contact commitments or conflict with manual recovery actions.
S217: Continuity modes are declared by the Mission Control Center after consultation with the affected technical leads and are recorded with the operational objective, expected duration, and exit criteria.
S218: In monitor-only mode, command release is stopped, telemetry reception continues where safe, and engineering teams focus on stabilizing observability and protecting evidence.
S219: In essential-service mode, the ground segment prioritizes spacecraft safety contacts, time-critical telemetry capture, core orbit support, and protection of unrecoverable payload data.
S220: Primary Processing Cluster can pause nonessential production queues and reserve compute capacity for validated recovery runs from known-good inputs.
S221: If site degradation persists, processing work is transferred to Backup Processing Cluster only after input custody, software baseline, and operator authorization have been verified.
S222: Cross-site failover is coordinated through Ground Network Manager so that antenna allocation, network routing, firewall state, and contact schedules remain consistent.
S223: North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna are placed in the recovery plan according to current availability and the spacecraft contact priority.
S224: Long Term Archive remains the custody reference during degraded operations, and any delayed ingest or publication is reconciled before normal service status is restored.
S225: User Services Portal communicates confirmed service impacts in operational terms and avoids publishing speculative root cause information before the incident lead approves release.
S226: Recovery is accepted only when command authority is verified, telemetry and product flows are reconciled, security monitoring has returned to the approved baseline, and responsible teams have signed the incident record.
S227: Routine mission service begins only after the operational readiness review confirms that ground procedures, staffing rosters, monitoring views, and escalation paths are under configuration control.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
